items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: But Budd Johnson was on that band.

ctx.x: He came in. And then the girl singer was Ida James: Ida was with Earl. There was another girl singer. I can't -- Madeline Green. I don't know if you remember her. She was with him too. But Budd Johnson was on that band. Ray Nance was on. In fact, Ray Nance was the guy who encouraged me to go with Lunceford. I wasn't going to go because I was having too much fun with Earl.

Earl's band was loose, you know, like no restrictions but Lunceford was -- you know, like you have to do this exactly like that. And, you know, when you're young you don't like -- you don't go for that too much, you know. And everything was just -- had to be just so and so.

items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: Trommy Young was in the band.

ctx.x: Benny Franklin's arm, and everything was all messed up. Trommy's foot and leg -- Trommy Young was in the band. Omar Simian, glass had flew all in his face. They had picked it out. See what -- they were working at the Orpheum Theater in St. Paul, Minnesota. And, what happened -- I don't know whose fault it was. It must have been the other truck's fault. They hit this bus. Because Fox got a lot of money and he hardly gave those guys a dime of that money.

Anyway, when I got into the theater opening day for them, they were all sitting up bandaged on the stage playing. Can you imagine that? That's a thing about the show must go on. All of these guys were up there. They had lost Cecil Irving. He's dead. And, a couple of them were half dead. And, Billy Franklin can't play. He was -- because his arm was all crushed up and everything. And, the rest of the buys had bandages all over their heads and faces and arms, and feet and big legs, sitting up there playing the show.…
